subject: Deal: Nimbus routing + audit requirements — prioritization request
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal ask: routing & audit requirements for Nimbus POC

Team —

Quick context: Nimbus Financial (large regional bank) is in final procurement for a POC -> enterprise contract. They’ve signaled verbally they will move to a committed Dedicated purchase (~$650k ARR) if we can meet two explicit engineering requirements before an in‑prod POC next quarter:

1) Per‑account routing policy: ability to pin/route requests for a customer to a specific model variant and region (they need a hard pin for a high‑accuracy variant during POC).
2) Extended audit logs & retention: token‑level attribution + request/response traces retained for 24 months and exportable in parquet/CSV for audits (they’re regulated).

Why this matters now: Nimbus expects delivery readiness as a gating condition for signing. Legal/procurement will not accept a go‑forward without those capabilities or firm mitigation. The mutual action plan (attached) shows the timeline: they want a kickoff call w/ security + engineering in 3 weeks, and target in‑prod POC within 8 weeks.

Ask: Can Product+Eng prioritize a scoped implementation (spike + MVP) so we can commit delivery dates in the MMP? If we can’t commit, we risk losing the deal or needing a large discount.

Notes / constraints:
- The customer is explicit about retention length (24 months) and format (parquet preferred).
- They require the routing policy to be API + Console driven.
- We may need to surface SLA exceptions for this account (latency/stability tradeoffs).

Attaching: nimbus-audit-reqs.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

Happy to sync with whoever owns infra — I can schedule a Tuesday 30‑min call with the Nimbus security lead if that helps.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0147

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal ask: routing & audit requirements for Nimbus POC

Thanks for the clear brief, Monica. High‑level questions before we scope:

- Acceptance criteria: for the routing pin, is the requirement that every single inference for Nimbus must use the pinned model (i.e. no fallback), or is a prioritized routing with fallback acceptable? Please paste the exact language procurement will sign off on.
- Audit retention: 24 months is a long tail. Do they need immediate searchable access or only export on request? Parquet export is straightforward but we need retention storage costs scoped.
- Timeline sensitivity: when do they expect the PO signed? You said 8 weeks to POC — do they expect full 24‑month retention from POC start or post‑contract?

Tentative ideas from product side:
- Spike to validate approach (API + console hooks) and storage impact: 2 weeks.
- Minimal MVP: routing API + a pinned model flag + exportable traces (short window retention + export job): ~6 weeks after spike, with infra effort for long‑term retention later.

We need business justification to allocate engineering headcount. Can you attach the customer email thread with procurement language and confirm deal economics (annual contracted revenue and likely discount asked)? Also, please include whether Nimbus requires region isolation (EU data residency would complicate).

Laura Bennett

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal ask: routing & audit requirements for Nimbus POC

Answering Laura’s questions inline:

- Routing acceptance: procurement wants a contractual statement that "all production traffic from Nimbus for the POC will be pinned to the agreed model variant and region; fallbacks are permitted only with prior written consent." So they want a hard pin for the POC period.
- Retention access: they want searchable access for audit investigations (eDiscovery style) and periodic exports. Prefer immediate access for security team, but we can negotiate export‑first if searchability is infeasible short term.
- Timeline / PO: They expect a signed PO within 6 weeks if we can provide committed delivery dates; if we can’t, they’ll push for a competitive alternative.
- Region: US only for this customer.

Deal economics: ~$650k ARR expected, potential upsell to additional regions after POC. Procurement is already asking for a list of security controls (I can share the procurement PDF).

Next step: I can set up a joint call with Nimbus security/compliance and our infra folks on Monday next week (I’ll coordinate calendars).

—Monica

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal ask: routing & audit requirements for Nimbus POC

Appreciate the detailed ask. Technical read and constraints:

Summary: two pieces — (A) per‑account hard routing/pin, (B) extended token‑level traces retention/export. Both are doable but non‑trivial.

Proposed technical plan (MVP):
- Spike (2 weeks): prototype routing flag (per‑customer config in control plane) + small‑scale trace exporter to S3/parquet; verify cost and performance impact.
- MVP (6–8 weeks post‑spike): API + console UI for pinning, enforcement in serving proxy, and an export pipeline for traces.

Estimates & resourcing: 2 backend engineers (serving/control plane), 1 infra engineer for storage/export & retention policies, 1 product PM support. Effort ~320 engineer hours for MVP.

Risk notes:
- Hard pin removes automatic model fallback that preserves stability — we’ll need a customer‑approved fallback policy for incidents.
- Token‑level traces at scale multiply storage and egress costs; 24 months retention will be a material OPEX line. We need a funded commitment or cost recovery plan.

Deliverables we need from Sales:
- Signed PO or explicit signed commitment to fund the engineering allocation (we can do an internal 2‑week spike on goodwill, but MVP requires business funding).
- Exact legal language for the routing guarantee (we’ll review for feasibility).

I’m attaching a short arch‑proposal draft I’ll iterate on if you want.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Deal ask: routing & audit requirements for Nimbus POC

Decision / next steps:

1) Approve a scoped 2‑week spike to validate approach and measure cost impact. Dev will lead the spike. Budget for spike approved from product discretionary.
2) Sales to secure a signed LOI or PO commitment before we schedule full MVP work. Monica — please move procurement to sign an LOI that confirms expected delivery windows.
3) Deliverables for spike (2 weeks):
   - Prototype control plane flag + basic enforcement test harness
   - Sample trace export to S3 in parquet with cost estimate for 24‑month retention
   - Short risks doc and fallback policy options
4) If spike outcomes are positive, Product will scope MVP effort and cost. Any additional headcount for >8 week work must be funded by the deal or pulled from roadmap with leadership approval.

Monica: please capture the concession (timelines + any credits) in HubSpot and attach procurement language. Karthik — can you help with customer success plan for the POC? Hannah — be prepared to run compliance walkthrough with Nimbus.

I’ll add a 30‑minute check‑in for EOD Friday next week to review spike progress.

Thanks — Laura
